base_properties.human_readable: Negotiated Overlapping-Consensus Floor for AI Governance (Pluralist-Pragmatic Reading)
base_properties.topic_domain: theological ethics / technology governance / political economy

stakeholders.name: leading_technology_states
stakeholders.situation: Convene and fund the multilateral AI governance process, draft treaty language, and chair the working groups. Their regulatory models and dignity vocabularies anchor the negotiated floor, and their firms gain certified access to partner markets. They can decline any single framework and build regional or bilateral alternatives instead.

stakeholders.name: major_frontier_labs
stakeholders.situation: Build and deploy frontier AI systems. They staff consultations, supply the technical expertise that drafts standards, and receive predictable compliance rules plus public legitimacy from participating. Compliance costs are real but priced against market access and reputational cover; compute location and incorporation jurisdiction are movable.

stakeholders.name: multilateral_governance_secretariat
stakeholders.situation: Administers the negotiation calendar, drafts compromise texts, and runs the review mechanisms. Depends on member-state contributions and consensus goodwill; its career staff identify with the continuation of the process itself. Exiting would mean dissolving the venue.

stakeholders.name: established_moral_traditions
stakeholders.situation: Well-resourced religious institutions and secular ethical bodies holding permanent consultative status. Their dignity vocabularies enter preambles and recitals, and their educational networks deliver compliance training. Full doctrinal specificity is traded away in compromise language; withdrawing from the table would contradict their self-understanding as dialogue partners.

stakeholders.name: diplomatically_weak_states
stakeholders.situation: Hold formal votes but rarely set agendas; they depend on technology transfer, aid flows, and market access from the convening powers. They accept floors calibrated elsewhere and field delegations a fraction the size of the drafting chairs. Leaving the framework would forfeit trade preferences and technical assistance.

stakeholders.name: indigenous_data_sovereignty_communities
stakeholders.situation: Communities whose collective and relational conceptions of dignity do not map onto individual-rights defaults. Consultation reaches them late and thinly; consent protocols and data-governance rules arrive pre-shaped. Their practical recourse is objection after adoption rather than drafting before it.

stakeholders.name: small_jurisdiction_ai_vendors
stakeholders.situation: Compliance costs scale with headcount while agenda access scales with diplomatic weight; they implement standards they took no part in writing. Serving domestic markets alone rarely sustains the business, so abandoning global channels is costly.

stakeholders.name: global_public_subject_to_ai_systems
stakeholders.situation: Receive the safety, transparency, and accountability minimums the negotiated floor guarantees wherever they live. The standards are negotiated over their heads; the specific harms they experience are aggregated into indicators they do not choose. Individual recourse is limited; collective consumer pressure is their main lever.

stakeholders.name: communitarian_dignity_traditions
stakeholders.situation: Traditions whose dignity concepts center duty, lineage, or cosmic order rather than individual-rights talk. They lack consultative credentials and translation resources, so their objections surface in side events and journals rather than negotiating rooms.

stakeholders.name: independent_ai_ethics_researchers
stakeholders.situation: Academic and civil-society analysts who track which proposals survive successive drafting rounds, audit compliance claims, and publish the gap between stated inclusion and actual agenda control. Funded variously by states, foundations, and universities; they hold no vote anywhere.

six_questions.coordination_function: Provides a workable common floor for regulating AI that crosses jurisdictions and value systems: safety, transparency, and accountability minimums that enough distinct traditions can accept, so developers face one negotiated baseline instead of fragmenting into incompatible national regimes, and so no community must first win a metaphysical dispute before any regulation becomes possible.
six_questions.transfer_function: Moves standard-setting authority and agenda control toward the states and institutions that convene and fund the negotiations; moves compliance costs onto smaller jurisdictions and thinly-staffed traditions; converts the distinctive normative claims of low-power traditions into diluted compromise language drafted elsewhere.
six_questions.absent_voices: Communitarian and duty-centered dignity traditions would object that the procedure's accepted formats translate their claims into rights-talk they do not recognize, but they hold no consultative credentials. Informal-sector workers governed by algorithmic management systems and future generations inherit the floor's choices without seats; dissent currently lives in side events, not negotiating rooms.
six_questions.disappearance_rationale: If the negotiated floor and its enforcement machinery vanished overnight, AI governance would fragment into competing blocs with incompatible requirements: developers lose the single baseline, diplomatically weak states lose the only protection they can reach, and cross-border deployment proceeds under whatever regime the deploying power prefers.
six_questions.founding_problem: Postwar rights architecture presumed a shared dignitarian core; border-crossing AI deployment exposed that no agreed content existed, and regulators needed a basis for common rules that did not require settling metaphysical disputes first.
six_questions.founding_problem_corroboration: Attested from outside the beneficiary set by Global South digital-sovereignty coalitions demanding stronger floors, by indigenous-caucus statements filed during treaty negotiations, and by independent governance scholarship documenting the gap between inclusion rhetoric and agenda control; the convening powers' own ratification debates concede the underlying coordination problem persists.

commentary.narrative_context:
AI development crosses every jurisdiction and every value system, but no culture or tradition owns a settled definition of human dignity. This story authors the pluralist-pragmatic answer: AI systems must clear a negotiated floor of safety, transparency, and accountability standards assembled from what sufficiently many traditions can accept, imposed by multilateral treaty and multi-stakeholder machinery, with no comprehensive doctrine written into the rules. The arrangement genuinely solves a coordination problem — it gives developers one baseline and gives weak states the only protection they can reach — while the same negotiation structure concentrates agenda control in the convening powers and dilutes the claims of traditions without geopolitical weight. The claim and the metrics are independent authored facts: the constraint is CLAIMED as tangled_rope from the authoring seat, and the metrics describe its actual operation; the engine computes each seat's classification from the structural data.

KEY AGENTS (by structural relationship):
- leading_technology_states: primary agenda-setter (institutional/arbitrage) — convenes, funds, drafts; can exit into regional alternatives
- major_frontier_labs: beneficiary with secondary agenda-setting pull (powerful/arbitrage)
- multilateral_governance_secretariat: administering agenda-setter (institutional/constrained)
- established_moral_traditions: beneficiary (organized/identity_locked) — vocabulary enters texts, doctrinal specificity traded away
- diplomatically_weak_states: primary target (moderate/trapped)
- indigenous_data_sovereignty_communities: primary target (powerless/trapped)
- small_jurisdiction_ai_vendors: target (moderate/constrained)
- global_public_subject_to_ai_systems: beneficiary with secondary payer exposure (organized/constrained)
- communitarian_dignity_traditions: excluded voice (powerless/trapped)
- independent_ai_ethics_researchers: analytical observer (moderate/analytical)
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness is authored moderate (0.50 at interval end) because the floor delivers real protection while the negotiation structure lets agenda holders calibrate its content and pace; the series rises monotonically as soft ethics charters hardened into binding instruments whose drafting rooms the convening powers dominate. Suppression (0.45) is authored as a RAW structural property — the engine scales only extractiveness by directionality and scope — reflecting treaty lock-in, market-access conditionality, and delegation-capacity asymmetry rather than overt coercion. Theater_ratio starts high (0.55 in 2016: principle summits, ethics boards, and consultations that absorbed input without effect) and declines as instruments acquired teeth, ending at 0.40: the functional share grew faster than the performative share, though multi-stakeholder consultation remains partly absorptive. Accessibility_collapse (0.38) is low because alternatives persist — national AI acts, regional bloc rules, and voluntary regimes all remain viable alongside the floor. Resistance (0.50) is real but non-terminal: sovereignty pushback, industry lobbying, faith-community objections, and Global South demands for stronger floors slow the machinery without breaking it. All three metric series run on one shared six-point time grid; the 2026 endpoints are marked projected.
commentary.perspectival_gap: From the agenda-setter seats (leading_technology_states, secretariat), the arrangement IS the coordination it built: a hard-won floor nobody could have legislated unilaterally, experienced as rope-like. From the payer seats the identical structure operates as enforced extraction: standards written elsewhere, consultation arriving late, compliance billed by headcount while agenda access bills by diplomatic weight. The sharpest divergence is lateral and same-level: diplomatically_weak_states and leading_technology_states are formally equal sovereigns in the same forum, yet the former are trapped (exit forfeits aid and market access) while the latter hold arbitrage (any framework can be replaced by a regional one they write themselves) — identical nominal power, opposite effective positions. Major_frontier_labs versus small_jurisdiction_ai_vendors repeats the same split inside the industry tier: both pay compliance, only one helped write the rules. The engine computes these per-seat differences from power, exit, and role data; the authored claim does not adjudicate them.
commentary.directionality_logic: Beneficiaries derive low directionality (subsidized by the floor): convening states collect legitimacy rents and agenda control; labs collect certainty and cover; established traditions see their vocabularies ratified in exchange for doctrinal dilution; the general public receives the safety minimum. Victims derive high directionality: weak states, indigenous communities, and small vendors bear calibration and compliance costs without agenda return. One override is declared: major_frontier_labs sit at d=0.18 rather than near the pure-beneficiary end because they carry genuine binding compliance costs and cannot fully route around the floor — the derivation from the beneficiary declaration alone would understate their cost-bearing. No override is declared for diplomatically_weak_states: the structural derivation (victim declaration, trapped exit, moderate power) places them near the target end, slightly above their true position since they do receive the floor good; that residual is carried by the lcd_calibration_ambiguity omega rather than forced into the override surface. Observers and excluded voices feed no directionality computation.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The classification guards against mislabeling in both directions. Reading the arrangement as pure rope erases the identifiable payers — traditions whose claims are diluted and jurisdictions that comply without shaping; reading it as pure snare erases the genuine floor that weak states would lose first if it collapsed; tangled_rope holds both halves in one structure with active enforcement. On genealogy: the founding problem (governing AI without first settling the metaphysics of dignity) is still live, corroborated from outside the beneficiary set, so no dead-mandate mismatch fires and no zombie flag is expected. The mandate has not outlived its function and no sunset clause applies. Drift to watch is not theatrical decay (theater_ratio is falling) but extraction accumulation through agenda capture: if draft-text analysis shows the floor's content increasingly tracks convening-power preference, the payer seats' computed types slide toward harder extraction while the agenda-setter seats stay rope-flavored — the divergence the corpus exists to measure.
commentary.kernel_context: This story instantiates the pluralist_pragmatic reading of the human_dignity_ai_governance kernel: dignity-content for AI governance is contested across cultures, so legitimate rules arise from negotiated overlapping consensus rather than any single metaphysic. Sibling readings, each its own constraint story: magisterial_integralist_reading (dignity as ontological gift known through faith and reason; governance conforming to Magisterium interpretation), secular_humanist_reading (dignity grounded in rational autonomy and UDHR-style rights; democratic rather than religious authority), techno_optimist_reading (dignity enhanced through augmentation; governance minimized to enable innovation). This reading's epsilon refers to the standing negotiated-multilateral arrangement itself, assessed by this reading's own lights — never to the arrangements its siblings would build in its place.

omegas.question: This constraint is the pluralist_pragmatic instantiation of the human_dignity_ai_governance kernel; how would the magisterial_integralist, secular_humanist, or techno_optimist instantiations change the structural facts?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Generate the sibling stories and compare beneficiary/victim sets, epsilon, and authority grounding; the disagreement is located precisely in whose conception of dignity supplies the CONTENT of AI-governance standards.
omegas.impact: Under the magisterial reading the victim set shifts to conscience-objecting developers and secular states and the beneficiary set contracts to the teaching office; under techno-optimism victims become subjects of unconsented experimentation and beneficiaries collapse toward builders; under secular humanism extraction routes through majoritarian rights-talk. Epsilon and classification move accordingly per seat.
omegas.description: Committer structure: one reading of a four-reading kernel; records the reading instantiated and the structural delta each sibling would introduce.

omegas.question: Is the negotiated floor a genuine least-controversial minimum acceptable across traditions, or is its content systematically calibrated to the priorities of the convening powers?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Comparative analysis of successive draft texts tracking which proposals survive revision rounds, paired with delegate interviews across power tiers.
omegas.impact: If calibrated to the powerful, effective extraction at payer seats exceeds the moderate authored value and the arrangement trends toward capture; if genuinely minimal, a larger share of the measured extraction is the irreducible price of agreement among incompatible value systems.
omegas.description: Whether floor content tracks consensus-neutrality or agenda-holder preference; also carries the residual directionality uncertainty for diplomatically weak states.

omegas.question: Is procedural fairness without metaphysical privilege itself a parochial liberal-proceduralist commitment that quietly privileges traditions already shaped by rights-talk — and is the real kernel the negotiation process or the neutrality norm layered above it?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Test whether duty-centered and communitarian traditions can express their dignity claims in the process's accepted formats without translation loss, and whether they would ever recognize an outcome the procedure could yield; alternatively adopt the framing in which the neutrality norm itself is the kernel and re-run classification.
omegas.impact: If the procedure is parochial, the constraint's claimed even-handedness fails: suppressed traditions are extracted twice, once by the floor and once by the frame, raising effective suppression and pushing payer-seat classifications toward the full-target end. Under the alternative framing the authority structure reads as extraction-grounded rather than distributed.
omegas.description: Framing under-determination: procedural neutrality as neutral meta-rule versus as one metaphysical position among many; alternative cs framings yield different patterns.

omegas.question: Will multilateral AI governance enforcement continue maturing into binding compliance machinery, or stall as soft-law principles?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Track treaty ratification counts, dispute-panel caseloads, and whether market-access conditionality attaches to the negotiated floor over the next review cycles.
omegas.impact: Continued maturation validates the rising suppression_requirement trajectory authored here; stalling flattens it and shifts the constraint's persistence onto reputational mechanisms, lowering its coercive profile and softening payer-seat effective extraction.
omegas.description: Trajectory of the enforcement capacity behind the negotiated floor.

network.dual_formulation_note: 'Human dignity in AI governance' is one colloquial label spanning four structurally distinct governance claims; per the epsilon-invariance principle each is authored as its own story with its own epsilon, beneficiary/victim sets, and authority grounding, linked through this network edge set. This file instantiates the pluralist-pragmatic member, whose epsilon (0.50) is moderate because a real coordination function (a workable cross-tradition floor) and a real extraction channel (agenda capture and lowest-common-denominator dilution borne by low-power traditions) operate through the same enforcement structure. The siblings differ sharply: the magisterial member concentrates benefit in the teaching office and imposes doctrinal conformity; the secular-humanist member routes extraction through majoritarian rights-talk while grounding authority in democratic deliberation; the techno-optimist member minimizes restriction and displaces costs onto experiment subjects and third parties. Upstream/downstream coupling among the siblings runs through shared treaty venues and competing draft texts rather than through logical dependency.
